'''Bruce Rashad Thornton Jr.''' (born September 14, 2003) is an American [[basketball]] player for the [[Houston Rockets]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State Buckeyes]], where he finished his career as the program's all-time leading scorer.

==Early life==
Thornton was raised in [[Alpharetta, Georgia]] and attended [[Milton High School (Georgia)|Milton High School]], where he was a four{{endash}}year starter on the basketball team.<ref name="Gatorade">{{cite web|url=https://www.ajc.com/sports/high-school-sports-blog/miltons-thornton-named-gatorade-boys-basketball-player-of-year/YAKKGMYMLJBKPOVQ5DMXUHSUOM/|first=Todd|last=Holcomb|title=Milton’s Thornton named Gatorade Boys Basketball Player of Year|website=AJC.com|access-date=2023-11-17|archive-date=2023-11-17|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231117002022/https://www.ajc.com/sports/high-school-sports-blog/miltons-thornton-named-gatorade-boys-basketball-player-of-year/YAKKGMYMLJBKPOVQ5DMXUHSUOM/|url-status=live}}</ref> The team won the state championship in 2021,<ref name="Gatorade" /><ref name="Read">{{cite web|url=https://bvmsports.com/2021/10/04/allen-whitehart-and-the-milton-high-school-eagles-team-make-it-to-the-state-basketball-championship/|first=Carisbel|last=Guaramato|title=Allen Whitehart and the Milton High School Eagles team make it to the state basketball championship|website=BVMSports.com|access-date=2023-11-17|archive-date=2023-11-17|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231117002025/https://bvmsports.com/2021/10/04/allen-whitehart-and-the-milton-high-school-eagles-team-make-it-to-the-state-basketball-championship/|url-status=live}}</ref> and Thornton was [[Mr. Georgia Basketball]]<ref>{{cite tweet|number=1507517153037238272|user=ATLTipoffClub|author=Atlanta Tipoff Club|access-date=May 31, 2022|title=Add Mr. Georgia Basketball to his resume ✅ Congratulations to @OhioStateHoops signee, @Bruce2T_ for having an outstanding season and taking home the ATOC Mr. Georgia Basketball award 🏀}}</ref> and the Gatorade Georgia Boys' Basketball Player of the Year in 2022.<ref name="Gatorade" />

===Recruiting===
Thornton was considered a consensus four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] by [[ESPN]], [[247Sports.com|247Sports]] and [[Rivals.com|Rivals]]. On November 26, 2020, Thornton committed to play college basketball for [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]] over offers from teams such as [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]], [[Georgia Bulldogs men's basketball|Georgia]], and [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.elevenwarriors.com/ohio-state-basketball-recruiting/2020/11/118547/four-star-point-guard-bruce-thornton-commits-to-ohio-state?amp|first=Colin|last=Hass-Hill|title=Four-Star Point Guard Bruce Thornton Commits To Ohio State|website=ElevenWarriors.com|access-date=2023-11-17|archive-date=2023-11-17|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231117002024/https://www.elevenwarriors.com/ohio-state-basketball-recruiting/2020/11/118547/four-star-point-guard-bruce-thornton-commits-to-ohio-state?amp|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite tweet|number=1332004279863873539|user=SUVtv|author=SUVtv|access-date=November 16, 2023|title=🚨ICYMI, Bruce Thornton has committed to Ohio State University}}</ref>

==Professional career==
On June 24, 2026, Thornton was selected by the [[New York Knicks]] with the 31st overall pick in the [[2026 NBA draft]] then was immediately traded to the [[Houston Rockets]] for pick 39 ([[Jack Kayil]]).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/news/knicks-rockets-trade-second-round-2026-nba-draft|title=Knicks open second round of 2026 Draft with swap of No. 31 overall|website=nba.com|date=June 25, 2026|access-date=July 19, 2026}}</ref>
